clue.text: He absorbs everyone in an East German capital

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: taken as written
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A man takes in the whole population of an East German city.
explanation.walkthrough: HALLE was a district capital in the former East Germany (GDR).
explanation.definitionFit: Halle on the Saale was the seat of one of the administrative districts of the GDR.

clue.text: Jolly occasion long overdue?

explanation.surface: A party that should have been held ages ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A high old time is a jolly occasion, and 'it's high time' says something is overdue.

clue.text: Lame little rascal in the heather

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, as the rascal is in the heather

parts.note: ling is a common name for heather
an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A naughty child with a bad leg sits among the moorland plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking lamely is limping, a synonym in adjective use.

clue.text: Yeomanry officer age about ten!

indicators.note: about means around, so the age wraps round the ten

parts.note: an eon is an age
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A cavalry officer's age is given as roughly ten.
explanation.walkthrough: An exon is one of four officers of the Yeomen of the Guard, the British royal bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yeomen of the Guard have officers titled exons, a specialist rank.

clue.text: Set upon, the animal suffered

parts.note: the ass is a donkey
ailed means was unwell, suffered

explanation.surface: Attacked, the poor beast was in a bad way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being attacked is being assailed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lose face by using the wrong make-up?

definitions.text: Lose face by using the wrong make-up?

parts.words: Lose face by using the wrong make-up?
parts.note: a botched cosmetic job literally ruins the look of one's face, which is the idiom for losing reputation

explanation.surface: A badly chosen foundation ruins someone's appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaging one's public reputation is the idiom, here read as literally ruining a made-up face.

clue.text: Top secret anthropoid

parts.note: an anthropoid is a great ape
X marks the unknown, something secret

explanation.surface: A classified file on a great ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top secret' reads as a single phrase; 'Top' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point, the summit.

clue.text: Exact reconstruction of neer tiller

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Exact reconstruction of neer tiller': the anagram fodder for LITERAL should be 'a tiller' (ATILLER); 'neer' is an OCR garble too far from 'a' to repair and no scan is held.

clue.text: Fools about 30

indicators.note: about signals the letters being turned around and rearranged

parts.note: 30 refers to the answer at 30 across

explanation.surface: Idiots, numbering roughly thirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about 30' reads as an approximate number; it is the anagram of the 30 across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopes are stupid people, a slang synonym.

clue.text: A figure of speech, as it were

definitions.text: A figure of speech, as it were

parts.words: A figure of speech, as it were
parts.note: a figure of speech is usually a rhetorical device, but here it is a literal figure, a doll, that seems to speak

explanation.surface: A remark on a rhetorical device, like a metaphor.
explanation.definitionFit: The doll on a performer's knee is a figure that appears to talk.

clue.text: Get stuck into the sport, by gum!

indicators.note: into places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a game is a sport
to bog down is to get stuck

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to throw themselves into the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by gum!' looks like an exclamation; gum is the definition. Gamboge is a yellow gum resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a gum resin from Asian trees used as a yellow pigment.

clue.text: Dance apace

explanation.surface: Dance quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a ballroom dance, and a single pace is one step.

clue.text: Gratuity about right for the journey

indicators.note: about means around, so the tip goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: A tip with roughly the right amount for travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a journey, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Even so, it's back a couple of lengths

indicators.note: back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
L is the abbreviation for length, so two of them

explanation.surface: Despite that, it is behind by two lengths in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Still' as an adverb means nevertheless, all the same.

clue.text: Greek god renowned in war, especially

indicators.note: in tells us the god's name lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: A Greek deity famous for his feats in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Ares is the Greek god of war, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares was the Greek deity of battle, famed for warfare.

clue.text: Post novel to the Spanish

parts.note: novel means new
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Send a book to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a verb; it is the definition, a staircase post.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the central upright or end post of a staircase.

clue.text: She's something special to a man of letters

parts.note: a gem is something prized
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree whose holder has letters after his name

explanation.surface: A woman is dear to a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemma is a girl's given name, standing for any female.

clue.text: Irresistible pointer up North

parts.note: an attractive indicator that always aims northward, as on a compass

explanation.surface: A charming finger raised towards the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass's magnetised pointer swings to point north.

clue.text: Emphasised keeping one's hair on, up to a point

indicators.note: in a down clue, up to puts the point on top of what follows

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
tressed means having tresses, keeping one's locks

explanation.surface: Someone stayed calm only to a certain extent under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping one's hair on' is the idiom for staying calm, but here it means having tresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A stressed syllable is one given emphasis.

clue.text: Clearly no mean sum

parts.note: no mean read as not stingy, so a lavish quantity

explanation.surface: Obviously not an average total in arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean here is stingy, so not mean is open-handed, a lavish quantity.

clue.text: Scholar taking ages to tot up

parts.note: eras are ages

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: to tot up is to sum

explanation.surface: A scholar takes ages to add up the figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Erasmus was the Dutch Renaissance humanist scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a celebrated Renaissance humanist and scholar.

clue.text: Sue's sly Latinised version of a Greek hero

indicators.note: a version is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman's cunning rendering of a Homeric hero in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses is the Latin name for Odysseus, so 'Latinised' also fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus, hero of the Odyssey, was called Ulysses by the Romans.

clue.text: Bird often found in pipes

explanation.surface: A bird that turns up in drainpipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cormorant-like seabird is a shag, and coarse shredded tobacco smoked in pipes is shag.

clue.text: Cross line in a letter that backfires

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Cross line in a letter that backfires': the only parse takes FIRES from inside 'backfires' and reverses it on 'back' from the same word, so one clue word is both fodder and indicator.
annotationWithheld.clue: Cross line in a letter that backfires

clue.text: See 9
It played its part in early recitals

indicators.note: in tells us the instrument lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: An instrument featured in ancient performances.
explanation.walkthrough: The lyre accompanied early Greek recitation, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is a harp-like instrument used to accompany recitation.

clue.text: Plant from river in marshy land

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, the river in the marsh

parts.note: a fen is marshland

explanation.surface: A plant taken from a river in the marshes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a flowerless plant with fronds.

clue.text: Find fault with fish

explanation.surface: Complain about the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain pettily, and the carp is a freshwater fish.

clue.text: No good for drinking but, as you see, they're useful

definitions.text: No good for drinking but, as you see, they're useful

parts.words: No good for drinking but, as you see, they're useful
parts.note: ... with no rim are useless as tumblers, but as spectacles they help you see

explanation.surface: Vessels that won't hold a drink but serve a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Frameless spectacles are useless for drinks but help eyesight.

clue.text: See 27
Paradoxical quality of dye that doesn't run?

definitions.text: Paradoxical quality of dye that doesn't run?

parts.words: Paradoxical quality of dye that doesn't run?
parts.note: a colour that stays put is called fast, though fast normally means quick

explanation.surface: A puzzle about colours that stay in the wash.
explanation.definitionFit: Colourfastness is a dye's resistance to running, while fast also means speedy.

clue.text: Presented a problem by taking a stand

explanation.surface: Made difficulties by adopting a firm position.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose a question is to present it, and to pose is to adopt a stance.
